WHY AI STOCKS ARE IMPLODING

The current implosion in so many stocks isn’t necessarily because their earnings are terrible. It’s because of how the market is reacting to and interpreting those earnings.

All of this reflects a shift in sentiment of the market participants, not some seismic shift in the fundamentals over the last few months.

The real question is whether all the stocks that were exploding higher in the spring ($INTC $SNDK $SMH $DRAM) should have been trading at those valuations in the first place.

Was sentiment far too euphoric back then? Or is the current sentiment far too bearish?

No idea and it’s not my job to know. Only time will tell.

My job is to recognize these shifts in sentiment through price action and technicals, and position myself to ride them.

Whether the market is being rational or irrational, I want to be on the right side of the move.

So what exactly does that mean? And perhaps more importantly, what doesn’t it mean?

First, no trader knows what’s going to happen. Everything is probabilistic at best and total noise at worst. But there are specific moments in time when the odds can become meaningfully skewed in one direction.

I personally think there's a pretty significant dislocation happening in market right now and this week gave me some of clearest evidence yet.

Both $GOOGL and $AMZN are planning to spend even more on AI infrastructure in 2027 after already investing record amounts this year with Andy Jassy even calling AI “a once in a lifetime opportunity” and making it clear Amazon has no plans to slow down.

Putting my corporate strategy hat back on I think market is overlooking something pretty important about Google because it can no longer simply decide AI is getting too expensive and go back to its traditional Search business when AI is now threatening very product that generates most of its profits.

That means infrastructure spending is becoming just as much about defending its existing business as capturing new growth which makes these investments much harder to pull back on even if investors become increasingly concerned about returns.

And that's what makes this selloff so interesting because market is punishing the companies writing the checks while those same companies are telling us they'll write even bigger ones next year.

I absolutely expect next phase of AI to become more selective with clear winners and losers but I don't think that means the infrastructure cycle is ending which is why I plan to keep adding to my highest conviction names across AI power, AI inference and Agentic AI.

Welcome to the Weekly KAOS — UrbanKaoboy’s end-of-week roundup covering Macro and Geopolitics, where I try and tease out the most impactful bits of the week.

Themes of the Week

The AI trade finally cracked this week, tech tumbled and bonds rallied into the growth scare, which is the Bullwhip snapping upstream and the Credit Canary singing louder.

Anyone who has studied supply chains knows the Bullwhip Effect, where a modest wiggle in end demand gets amplified as it travels upstream, so that a 5% bump at the retailer can balloon into a 40% swing at the factory. As I posted this week, I am not nearly smart enough to know how the AI/Anthropic story ends, but the Bullwhip Effect really concerns me.

Weekly KAOS - The Bullwhip & The Canary

A small wobble in end demand snaps hardest UPSTREAM where the chips, data centers and power sit, and because that upstream now runs on Debt rather than Equity, Credit is the Canary in the Coalmine.

Welcome to the Weekly KAOS — UrbanKaoboy’s end-of-week roundup covering Macro and Geopolitics, where I try and tease out the most impactful bits of the week.

Themes of the Week

The AI trade finally cracked this week, tech tumbled and bonds rallied into the growth scare, which is the Bullwhip snapping upstream and the Credit Canary singing louder.

Anyone who has studied supply chains knows the Bullwhip Effect, where a modest wiggle in end demand gets amplified as it travels upstream, so that a 5% bump at the retailer can balloon into a 40% swing at the factory. As I posted this week, I am not nearly smart enough to know how the AI/Anthropic story ends, but the Bullwhip Effect really concerns me.

Everyone is frothing over that parabolic ARR and forgetting that Anthropic sits near the FRONT of the Bullwhip, while the truly capital-hungry links, the chips, the servers, the gigawatts, sit far UPSTREAM. That is exactly where a small crack at the handle becomes a violent snap at the tip.

What makes the Bullwhip dangerous rather than merely interesting is how that upstream is now financed. The buildout has shifted from Equity “funny money” to Debt, so the first place a slowdown shows up is not the stock tape but Credit. I laid out the mechanics in my Wile E. Coyote piece. If Equity is a Long Call on the Firm’s Assets, then Debt is a Short Put on those same Assets, which is why CREDIT is a far better canary than the VIX, because Short Puts feel deteriorating Asset Value before anyone else does.

That canary has been singing since last week’s Weekly KAOS, when CoreWeave’s CDS implied better-than-even odds of default while its stock still carried a roughly $35B price tag. This week it sang louder, with CoreWeave bonds north of 15% and the long end rallying hard as the growth scare took hold. The same physics runs under my Wile E. Coyote Equity market, and it ran through nearly every thread this week, even as Oil ripped to six-month highs on Gulf escalation and China kept probing on chips and minerals.

How to Survive a Market Correction.

I wrote this 4 years ago but it's still relevant today.

Hi everyone,

With the market in correction, I thought I'd discuss five things you should be doing during this time to set yourself up for success when the next uptrend comes along. Corrections are a natural part of the market cycle and will create fantastic opportunities down the line. We just have to be ready.

1. Stay optimistic and flexible.

Corrections are a volatile and frightening occurrence for new investors and traders. However, they are common and a natural part of the stock market cycle. The important thing is to stay calm and follow your investing or trading plan. 

If you are an investor and use DCA, your timeframe and strategy depend on you carrying on with business as usual. 

As a trend follower and trader, you want to follow your risk management system and protect yourself during volatile and corrective periods by exiting when the trend changes.

Personally, I turn to mostly cash when the market breaks the 21 EMA and 50 SMA, market leadership breaks down, and we see other signs of institutional distribution such as breakouts failing. 

The key is to stay calm and follow your process objectively.

It is also important to stay optimistic and to remember that corrections set up the best opportunities in the market. The deeper the correction, the better.

The depth of the March 2020 correction facilitated a fantastic year for growth traders. As the market rebounded from a 30% correction, many growth names rose 200%, 300%, even 500%. When a correction occurs, stay optimistic and think about the amazing new leaders that will rise from the ashes.

Zoom was a great example of correction growth in 2020. It showed RS early on in the correction and went on a fantastic run of over 300% once the market pressure lifted.

Additionally, it is important to stay flexible during a correction. Market conditions can change sharply, and we have to be ready when we identify positive character changes such as follow-through days. 

Keep following your market routines and stay on top of potential leaders that show accumulation signs during the market decline. This homework will serve you well when the uptrend begins. The market trend can shift in just a matter of days, so you need to be ready with a buy list when we see groups shape up and the indexes follow through.

2. Protect mental and financial capital.

During a correction, it's very important that you protect both your mental and financial capital. As traders, we have to accept that sometimes the absolute best thing we can do is sit on our hands and do nothing. No strategy works 100% of the time, and if you employ a trend-following strategy similar to CANSLIM, you need to understand that choppy and corrective markets will cause paper cut after paper cut if you try to get involved before a true uptrend emerges.

This gradual drawdown will not only cut into your account balance but will also leave you disheartened and unwilling to act when the trend actually changes. You have to recognize that your trading style has its own optimal environment. 

For me, this is often when the QQQ and growth-focused ETFs like the IWO are trending above rising 21 EMAs. If it is not your optimal environment, then you must realize that the probabilities are stacked against you and you are trading merely for action instead of wealth. Know what your environment looks like in terms of the action of the indexes as well as setups and leadership stocks.

quoted.text:
I went through the on-chain data on the $6.3B Binance hack. What most people are posting is WRONG, and the smartest part of this attack is getting no coverage…

The main drain took 24 SECONDS. Not 20 minutes. About $2.7B left two Binance Ethereum wallets in under half a minute.

How they got in:

Binance says a DevOps engineer's laptop "may" have been compromised. They also say there is no evidence a private key leaked. Both can be true, and that's the interesting part.

An EIP-7702 delegation needs a valid signature from the wallet. If you control a service container that is already authorised to request signatures, you never need the key. You just ask the signing service to sign for you. Same shape as Bybit, where attackers hit a developer machine at Safe.

The transaction itself:

A type-4 tx carrying 50 separate EIP-7702 authorizations, all for the Binance 14 hot wallet, all pointing at the same attacker contract.

Only ONE landed. Nonce range 18,914,775 to 18,914,824.

They didn't know the wallet's exact nonce, so they sprayed a range and let one hit. Blockaid caught this.

The part nobody is talking about:

Within 3 minutes the attacker supplied 60M USDT to Aave as collateral and borrowed 19,762 wETH against it. About $45M.

Tether froze the address right after. Aave froze the markets 46 minutes later.

TOO LATE. They had already turned freezable stablecoins into ETH nobody can touch. Marc Zeller confirmed the position is overcollateralised so Aave isn't out anything.

I traded CDS from the start in the late ’90s. Buyers were never the problem. Sellers were. 🧵

1) Banks hedged derivative counterparty risk and freed up RBC on undrawn revolvers, convert arbs hedged credit, and L/S funds went short. Long-only asset managers wouldn’t sell unless the basis was fat.

2) Synthetic CDOs fixed that. We built diversified IG CDS portfolios and got shadow ratings on the tranches. AIG FP and the ilk just wanted “high spread” for a AA or AAA. Then CDX tranching made sellers plentiful, and they were diamond hands who ignored marks. Volumes exploded. 

3) That seller died in the GFC, and CDS volumes collapsed. Now hyperscalers and chipmakers want to issue $1trn of GPU debt, and the CDS bid is massive. Who sells?

4) Asset managers should sell at a positive basis, but they haven’t yet. Pod PMs are the offer, and they aren’t diamond hands. 

Expect a thin offer side, wider spreads, and more vol.​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​

posts.name: Andy Constan
posts.text:
Growth trend 101.  

Two of the most basic tools one needs to trade macro are growth estimates.  They come in two general categories.  Economic data and Market pricing data.  Simplistically and broadly economic data is by definition  and in practice lagging based on lagging reporting and rear view mirror.   It is excellent in defining the trend of what has happened, it is modestly useful in spotting a shift in economic momentum but given its lagging nature is pretty bad at that and it is NOT useful for seeing the turn.  Market pricing is very noisy however it clearly stays ON trend and like economic data is able to see the trend in the rear view mirror.   However its noisiness creates falls turns in the economy.  Furthermore market based anti growth moves tend to elicit asymmetric responses by policymakers (fed reacts to any dip, fiscal ONLY cares about dips). BUT when a trend breaks and breaks for good and policymakers are unwilling or unable to act the market based indicators always beat the economic indicators.  Once again market based indicators of growth have flipped counter trend.  See highly simplistic but pretty good basic bond vs stock chart.  Is this noise?  Will Bessent act next week and we end up right back on trend.  More than likely.  The point of this tweet is that standalone economic trend and momentum signals will ALWAYS miss the turn.  You need forward looking ideas like " Not enough pie" I will pay you Tuesday  for a Hamburger today" and "no v top in interest rates to see the future AND both economic and market based data to see trends, counter trends and new trends

posts.name: Aaron Levie
posts.text:
It’s almost incomprehensible how wide the distance is between someone who’s working at the frontier with AI and basically everyone else right now. 

The crazy thing is these lines are not converging, but only growing farther apart. If the curve of AI progress had leveled off, it would certainly have given most people and companies time to catch up or implement their workflows in a standardized way. The technology would have neutralized competitive advantage because everyone would be using it the same way.

But what’s happened is the opposite. The curve of AI progress is basically going vertical right now, which means if you had codified your processes 3-6 months ago you’re likely already behind again. Now imagine most companies that kicked into gear a year ago and thought that they were done. Even further behind now.

I’ve never seen a technology in my life and career that improves at this rate, which consequently means you need to upgrade your expectations at a similar rate. Our brains weren’t wired for this, and our organizational change management processes certainly weren’t either.

With any form of recursive self improvement, things just get wilder. It’s a time when you will need to be constantly reevaluating the things that didn’t work just a couple months ago to see if they now can be solved. AI native companies certainly have a strong advantage due to this right now, so now it comes down to can the bigger companies keep up. Wild times.
